column1: # The published genus-level IS711 real-time PCR assay of
#   Bounaadja L., Albert D., Chenais B., Henault S., Zygmunt M.S., Poliak S., Garin-Bastuji B. (2009)
#   "Real-time PCR for identification of Brucella spp.: a comparative study of IS711, bcsp31 and per
#   target genes." Veterinary Microbiology 137:156-164. doi:10.1016/j.vetmic.2008.12.023, PMID 19200666.
# That paper is the answer key for a *repeat-targeted* assay: its subject is a multi-copy target, IS711,
# set against two single-copy ones, and IS711 won on sensitivity. IS711 is a 842-base insertion sequence
# (GenBank M94960) carried several times over by every Brucella genome and by nothing else.
# The paper is paywalled, so the three oligos are taken from the open-access papers that reproduce them
# and cite it. Eighteen of those in PMC carry the reverse primer as GGCCTACCGCTGCGAAT and one as
# CGCCTACCGCTGCGAAT; the second spelling is in no Brucella genome, so it is a typo in that one paper and
# the first is used here. `is711_census.py` locates all three in a genome before anything is run, which is
# how that was caught -- the same reason `validation/brucella/verify_amplicon.py` exists.
# amplicon_bp is **measured here, not quoted**: 63 bases between the outer 5' ends of the two primers, in
# every exact copy of the amplicon. The paper's own figure could not be read. `check_assay.py` prints it as
# "the paper reports", which for this one row means "measured". Measured in three complete genomes, which
# hold 3, 6 and 38 exact copies of it: GCF_000008145.1 (B. abortus bv. 1 str. 9-941 -- not 2308, as an
# earlier version of this comment said), GCF_000007125.1 (B. melitensis 16M, which is the one
# `is711_census.py` picks, being the first complete classical genome by accession) and GCF_000016845.1
# (B. ovis).
target
genus
